text: Geothermal heat flux from the crust is about ninety milliwatts per square metre
as_written: Geothermal heat also slows the collapse of the atmosphere. The air pressure fell only a fraction of a percent in the first week as water vapor condensed. Over the next two months the pressure continues to shrink very slowly, because the cold air can hold less water vapor and because the thin atmosphere loses heat to space faster than it can be replenished. The loss is on the order of a few parts per thousand, not enough to cause immediate suffocation, but it makes breathing harder for those already weakened.
source: U.S. Geological Survey, Heat Flow Data, 2020
